obligations.text: No pre-screen attestation is counted as an approval or a change request, and no pre-screen verdict ever admits a revision; at most it refuses, and only under a policy that opts in on the fail-closed path.
The prompt and guidelines a pre-screen is produced under are read from the base revision, never from the candidate the gated agent produced, and their digests are in the attestation.
The verdict is read from the review's structured verdict block only; output without a valid block is an error, never a verdict, and an error never approves.
A policy that opts in to refuse on a deny pre-screen also refuses when the pre-screen is missing, unreadable or for another revision; a policy that does not opt in evaluates exactly as spec 037 does.

Admission over a revision with a no-findings pre-screen and no approval refuses for the missing approval; a findings pre-screen under an opting policy refuses and under a default policy changes nothing; the spec 037 differential test still passes for every policy without the option.

record.summary: Records the managed AI review's verdict on a revision as an advisory attestation naming the model, the prompt's digest, the guidelines' digest and the structured verdict. It is shown beside statecraft/approval/v1 and is never counted as an approval. It may order a review queue. A policy may let a deny refuse admission only on a fail-closed path, where a missing or unreadable pre-screen refuses too. An AI deciding, confidence-gated auto-approval, approval on error, substring parsing of a verdict and a prompt the gated agent can influence are forbidden.
record.title: An AI pre-screen is an advisory attestation shown beside approvals and never counted as one
